full_judgment:
4. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rules, in brief, are that Pramathanath Das (since dead) was the owner and possessor of the huge property including a Cinema Hall named Ullasini situated at Khulna town. He executed and registered. a Will on 9-101945 in favour of his wife Molina Rani Dasi and grandson Prasanta Kumar Das. Pramathanath died in the year 1955 at Khulna town and the propounders of the said Will filed LA Case No. 4 of 1955 (Probate) in the Court of District Judge, Khulna under the provisions of Succession Act to get an order of letter of administration. Learned District Judge, Khulna by order passed on 30-3-1959 granted letter of Administration and Molina Rani and Sharadindu Bhusan Nandi were appointed as executors of the Will. Sharadindu Bhusan subsequently resigned from his post and the Court replaced there Sharat Chandra Saha, an Advocate. Molina Rani filed an application before the District Judge, 1Chulna on 13-12-1984 praying for appointing Mrinal Kanti Saha, petitioner No.1 in CR No.3093 of 1998, an Advocate as executor showing the unwillingness of executor Sharat Chandra to work. Learned District Judge allowed the prayer on 13-12-1984 and appointed him as one of the executors of the estate. He has been functioning as an executor subject to the control of the learned District Judge. Prashanta Kumar, one of the propounders of the Will did never come forward to take the charge of his share in terms of the Will. Consequently, Molina and the petitioner Mrinal Kanti jointly Continued to function as executors till Molina's death on 27-9-1996. In the rule petition it is further contended that the Government by notification dated 31-10-1965 and 29-11-1965 wanted to take over the management of the aforesaid cinema hall and other properties left by Pramathanath on the ground of its enlisting as enemy property under the provisions of Defence of Pakistan Rules. Against the aforesaid gazette notification Molina Rani and Sharadindu Bhusan filed two writ petitions bearing Nos.205 and 206 of 1966 before the High Court Division at Dhaka. Initially Rules were issued and finally those were made absolute by judgment and order passed on 12-5-1967 and the notifications of 1965 were declared illegal, ultra vires and not binding upon them. Against which the Government filed Leave Petitions 97D and 98D of 1967 before the Supreme Court of Pakistan but those were dismissed and the judgment and order pasked by the High Court Division in the writ petitions were affirmed. Thereafter, the administrators got back the possession of the property in 1968. Subsequently, the Vice Chairman of East Bengal Enemy Property Management Board issued another notice on 17-4-1968 directing Molina Rani to deposit 50% of the income of the estate stating that the part of its share had become enemy property by operation of law. By order dated 24-8-1968 the Vice Chairman sent copies to all concerned notifying 50% of share of Prasanta Kumar in the estate ignoring the judgment passed in writ petitions and affirmed by the Supreme Court. Molina Rani and Mrinal Mani then instituted Title Suit No.1177 of 1968 in the Court of First Munsif, Khulna against the Government praying for permanent injunction. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 28-11-1989 but the opposite parties did not challenge it before any Court. Petitioner 1 as administrator has been functioning by submitting audit account of the estate to the District Judge and depositing money to the banks Opposite party 1 herein, the Government at the behest of interested quarters submitted two applications on 15-2-1998, one praying for removing petitioner No.1 from administrator of the estate and the other to appoint a new administrator in his place and to drop the probate case and to release the fund deposited as well as the property to the Government. Learned District Judge by the impugned order rejected the said applications but made some observations against the executors and finally dropped the probate case. 

 7. Mr Subrata Saha, learned Advocate for the petitioners in Civil Revision No.3093 of 1998 and opposite parties 1-4 in Civil Revision NoA153 of 2015 submits that although learned District Judge, Khulna rejected the applications filed by the Government, but in the findings and ordering part made some remarks and finally dropped the probate proceedings which is against the provisions of law applicable in a probate case. Mr Saha then submits that while gazette notification was published declaring property under Will as enemy property, Molina Rani and another executor invoked writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division and Rules issued in two writ petitions were made absolute which were also affirmed by the then Supreme Court of Pakistan. Thereafter being threatened as to the enjoyment of the property Molina and another instituted a suit against the Government in the Court of the then Munsif, Khulna praying for permanent injunction. The suit was finally decreed, but the government did not challenge it before higher Court and the aforesaid decree is still binding upon them. Government at any time can take over any property complying with the provisions of section 92 of the SAT Act, but the learned District Judge in the impugned order passed opinion which will encourage to take the property under management and control on decided issue. The finding of the learned District Judge is contrary to its decision. Until or unless the heirs of Prashanta or Molina come forward to take over the property under Will it is to be managed by the executors appointed by the learned District Judge. In the aforesaid premises the Rule issued in Civil Revision No.3093 of 1998 would be made absolute and the impugned judgment and order is to be set-aside, on the other hand the Rule issued in Civil Revision 4153 of 2015 would be discharged because no probate for the Will executed by Molina is granted till today to petitioner Parikshit. 

 11. It transpires that in 1965 a part of the property was enlisted as enemy property and gazette notifications were published. Molina Rani and another executor then invoked writ jurisdiction in the then High Court at Dhaka in Writ Petition Nos. 205 of 206 of 1966 challenging the aforesaid gazette notifications. The rules issued in the aforesaid writ petitions were made absolute and the action of the Government declaring the property as enemy property was declared without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The Government although filed Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal Nos.97-D and 98-D of 1967 in the Supreme Court of Pakistan but both the petitions were dismissed summarily by elaborates judgment and the judgment passed by the High Court Division was affirmed. It further appears that, thereafter, the Government took attempt again to take over the management and control of the property by issuing two letters. Molina Rani and another then instituted Title Suit No.1177 of 1968 in the Court of the then Munsif, Khulna against the Government. The learned Assistant Judge after examining the plaintiffs' witnesses and considering the documents Exhibits 1-4 by its judgment and decree passed on 28-11-1989 decreed the suit ex-parte and the defendants, i.e., the Government has been restrained permanently by an order of injunction. The Government did not challenge the said judgment and decree before any Court. 

 12. In the probate proceeding the Government is neither a party nor it prayed for adding them so. The Government did not claim that they got the property from the testators. It further appears that the learned GP issued a certificate of power and accordingly the Deputy Commissioner filed two applications upon which the impugned order was passed which is under challenge in Civil Revision No.3039 of 1998. If the Government claims interest or wants to take management and control of any property, it can file a suit against the person or may add as defendant in the suit as per the provisions of Order 27, rule I of the Code. But neither the Government filed a suit nor prayed to add it as defendant in this case. It cannot file applications on the strength of so called certificate of power issued by the GP. Under the provisions of section 283 of, the Succession Act the Government being a third party to the Will cannot appear in the suit by filing an application making out a third case [Reliance placed on 33 DLR (AD) 254, 42 DLR (AD) 133]. Moreover, the judgment of the High Court at Dhaka passed in the Writ Petitions 205 and 206 of 1966 which were affirmed by the Supreme Court in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 97D and 98D of 1967 and lastly the decree passed by the Assistant Judge in Title Suit No.1170 of 1968 are still in force. 

 13. The finding of the learned District Judge is contradictory to its decision. If he is not authorized to entertain the applications filed by the Government, he cannot make any observation in disposing those. Undoubtedly, section 92 of the SAT Act provides extinguishment of the right of rayats in certain cases but section 92 is not applicable in the present case and here we are of the view that impugned order dated 21-5-1998 was passed by the District Judge in gross violation of the judgment and order passed by the High Court in the aforesaid writ petitions, the order on the leave petitions by the Supreme Court and the decree passed by the Assistant Judge in Title Suit No.1177 of 1968 which are still in force. Scrutinizing the applications filed by the Government and the order passed on those, it further appears that the applicant brought allegation that whereabouts of Prashanta could not be detected and he permanently resides in India. It is a vague allegation because, if any heirs of Prashanta or Pramathanath appear in future and claim the property by the strength of Will, then the appointed executors would be legally bound to act in accordance with the terms of the Will and they have to hand over the account and the property under Will to them. In the aforesaid discussion the 'question of dropping the probate proceeding does not make any sense. The District Judge passed such order violating the provisions of law at the instance of such a body who is not claiming under testator.
